It starts with one keystroke

Alt + X. Anywhere. Every time.

Open a small floating window right above whatever you were doing. It launches first, it stays reachable, and every icon you need sits in its header — clipboard, favorites, images, notes, snippets, folders. Most moments never need the full screen.

Press it again to hide the focused quick window. Closed the window? SnapNote waits in your system tray, so Alt+X works even when SnapNote is nowhere in sight.

Alt+Xshow it. Hide it. Keep moving.

A day you’ll recognise

Three small rescues, one quiet tool.

  1. 9:04 — Morning

    The address that arrived too early

    A friend sends a café address, then a train time, then a link — and your clipboard forgets all but the last. With automatic capture on, SnapNote keeps each one. Search “café” at the gate and breathe out.

  2. 14:20 — Afternoon

    The reply you keep rewriting

    The same thank-you note, the same status format, week after week. Save it once as a snippet with {{name}} and {{project}}. This time it takes eleven seconds, and it feels a little magical anyway.

  3. 22:47 — Late evening

    The screenshot full of numbers

    A chart someone pasted in a meeting. Pin it on screen, crop the region you need, and let local OCR pull the text out so it becomes searchable. Nobody had to open a spreadsheet at midnight.

Small rescues, all day — and not one of them left your machine.

Your workspace
Copy itFind itKeep it yours

Text, images, notes and reusable replies. One place to return to.

Clipboard with a memory

Text and images, deduplicated, searchable across titles, content, tags and text found inside images. A bounded history you decide the size of.

Notes that keep their shape

A real editor: headings, lists, tasks, code blocks, undo and redo. Your old notes migrate over untouched on first launch.

Snippets with blanks

Mark any text as a template with {{variables}}. Copying fills the blanks and leaves the original untouched.

Images, handled

Crop, annotate, extract text with local OCR, or pin an image above other windows while you work. Delete images from clips or notes whenever you choose.

Alt+X, everywhere

The small quick window with every icon in its header, one keystroke away — even straight from the system tray after you close the app.

Folders, sessions, favorites

Group a moment of research into a session, park a project in a folder, star what keeps coming back. Multi-select copies text across clips.

A vault, if you want one

Optional AES-256 encryption for the live workspace, instant lock, and password-protected backups you can take anywhere.

Privacy, in plain words

Your words stay yours.

SnapNote makes no account, cloud or telemetry requests. History lives in a transactional store inside the app’s own profile; nothing is uploaded because there is nothing to upload with.

Turn on lock-and-encryption and the workspace is rewritten with AES-256-GCM and PBKDF2 — the password exists only in your head. Backups can carry a password too, so a copy in your bag stays a secret.

A little more, honestly

Questions you’d actually ask.

Does Alt+X work if I closed the app?

If the window is closed, yes — SnapNote keeps running in the system tray and the shortcut brings the quick window straight back. If you chose Quit in the tray menu, the shortcut rests too; start SnapNote once and it is listening again.

Where does my data go?

Nowhere. Clips, notes and settings live in local, transactional storage inside the app’s profile on this device. There is no sync, no server, no analytics to send them to.

Why is OCR separate?

Text recognition uses Tesseract, and bundling someone else’s runtime silently didn’t feel ours to do. Install Tesseract once, add it to PATH, and SnapNote uses it for image text — extract it once and the text becomes searchable.

Is my old SnapNote data compatible?

Yes. On first launch your original rich-text notes are migrated into the new store, with a recovery copy of the old records kept during normal use. Storage problems surface in the app instead of being swallowed.

Windows only?

Windows 10 and 11 are where it is built and validated end to end. The code is Tauri-based and dreams of more, but today Windows is the honest answer.
